title: Freed SOAP note and patient summary
problem: Doctors spend excessive time converting patient conversations into structured documentation.
objective: Demonstrate a supervised transcript-to-note workflow and detect unsupported additions.
preparation: Open the official tool in a training account if available
Explain consent and local data rules
synthetic_input: Fictional consultation: Maya, age range 45–55, reports a dry cough for four days and mild fever yesterday. No chest pain or breathlessness. History includes controlled hypertension. Current medicine is listed only as 'one blood-pressure tablet'; drug and dose are unknown. Examination and vital signs were not supplied.
steps: Explain consent and data-protection requirements before recording or transcription.
Use only the supplied fictional transcript; do not record workshop participants.
Generate a patient-friendly summary with warning signs and when to contact a doctor.
Generate a referral or follow-up note without inventing examination findings.
Compare each statement with the transcript.
Highlight omissions, unsupported additions, and ambiguity around the medicine.
Discuss EHR transfer only as an approved institutional workflow.
sample_prompt: Create a SOAP-note draft from this fictional transcript. Do not add examination findings, diagnoses, medicines, doses, tests, or plans that are absent. Put unknowns under 'Information to verify'. Then draft a patient summary at approximately Grade 7 reading level with warning signs and a 'not a prescription' notice. End with a clinician-verification checklist.
expected_output: A structured draft note plus patient summary, with unknowns visible and no invented examination.
verification_points: Every symptom and time point matches the transcript
Medicine name and dose remain unknown
No diagnosis or normal examination was fabricated
Escalation advice is reviewed by a clinician
failure_modes: Invented vital signs or normal examination
debrief_questions: Which line was hardest to verify?
Would this draft change your clinical reasoning?
What must happen before EHR transfer?
safety_notice: Synthetic input only; qualified review required.

title: Heidi consultation-to-document workflow
problem: Clinicians need draft notes, follow-up documents, and patient summaries from the same consultation.
objective: Compare multiple document types against one source transcript.
synthetic_input: Fictional follow-up: Arjun, age range 55–65, has home blood-pressure readings between 142–154/86–94 over one week. He reports missing tablets twice. No acute symptoms are stated. Medicine name, clinic reading, examination, and laboratory results are absent.
steps: Explain consent and exclude real participant audio.
Generate the note and preserve missing fields.
Draft a follow-up letter without changing the plan.
Compare all documents with the same source.
Mark contradictions, additions, and lost uncertainty.
Discuss institutional approval before integration or storage.
sample_prompt: Using only this fictional hypertension follow-up, draft a structured note, a plain-language patient summary, and a follow-up letter. Do not infer a diagnosis, treatment change, or normal examination. List missing information and end each output with a verification checklist.
expected_output: Three source-consistent drafts with missing clinical information clearly labelled.
verification_points: Readings and adherence details remain exact
No medicine or dose is inferred
No treatment change is proposed
The patient version remains understandable
failure_modes: Treating home readings as a confirmed clinic diagnosis
debrief_questions: Which output needs the most clinical editing?
What should never be copied automatically?
safety_notice: Synthetic input only; qualified review required.

title: Perplexity PICO evidence brief
problem: A doctor needs a fast, source-linked orientation to a clinical or research question.
objective: Move from PICO to a checked evidence brief without treating generated citations as verified.
preparation: Have two primary sources ready for inspection
synthetic_input: PICO: In adults with uncomplicated hypertension in primary care (P), does home blood-pressure monitoring with clinician feedback (I), compared with usual clinic monitoring (C), improve blood-pressure control and adherence (O)?
steps: Convert the question into PICO form.
Search for recent guidelines, systematic reviews, and trials.
Inspect every cited source title and date.
Open at least two primary sources.
Record population, setting, and outcome definitions.
Check that citations support each statement.
State that the brief is orientation, not patient-specific advice.
sample_prompt: Answer the PICO question using recent source-linked evidence. Separate guidelines, systematic reviews, and primary trials. For each claim, provide the source and publication date. State population differences, limitations, and unresolved uncertainty. Do not invent citations.
expected_output: A dated, source-linked orientation with evidence types separated and uncertainties visible.
verification_points: Sources exist and titles match
Claims are supported by opened sources
Population and setting are relevant
Recency is not confused with quality
failure_modes: Reliance on summaries without opening papers
debrief_questions: What would you verify before clinical use?
safety_notice: Synthetic input only; qualified review required.

title: NotebookLM journal-club synthesis
problem: Doctors have several papers but limited time to prepare a journal club.
objective: Create a source-grounded comparison while checking every statement against authorised papers.
preparation: Use openly shareable or authorised papers
synthetic_input: Authorised source pack: three fictional study summaries on home blood-pressure monitoring, each with different populations, follow-up periods, and outcome definitions.
steps: Upload only authorised or openly shareable papers.
Extract population, intervention, comparator, outcomes, and limitations.
Generate a presentation outline or audio overview if available.
Verify all statements against the uploaded documents.
Record missing information rather than filling gaps.
sample_prompt: Using only the uploaded sources, create a table with design, population, intervention, comparator, outcomes, follow-up, risk of bias, and limitations. Cite the source name for every row. Identify disagreements without resolving them unless the source does. Draft six journal-club questions.
expected_output: A source-labelled comparison table, disagreement map, and journal-club discussion guide.
verification_points: Every cell traces to an uploaded document
Study designs are classified correctly
Absence of evidence is not described as no effect
Limitations remain study-specific
failure_modes: Treating source-grounded output as clinically correct
debrief_questions: Where did the studies genuinely disagree?
Would an audio overview be sufficient for appraisal?
safety_notice: Synthetic input only; qualified review required.
